Erin —

Thanks for the heads up and for flagging procurement. I pulled together a concise MAP that splits the work into three lanes: evaluation fixes, procurement/contract, and go‑live ops. Two options below:

Option A — Preserve Sep 30 (aggressive)
- Helium: prioritize the kernel patch validation (ETA 1 week), run smoke load on Canary cluster (2 days)
- Redwood: provide a precompiled fallback model variant and a 48‑hour on‑call window for rapid hotfixes
- Both: execute a negotiated SLA credit structure if we need to roll back

Option B — Rebaseline (conservative)
- Target go‑live Oct 14: provides a two‑week buffer for testing + procurement signoff
- Helium: freeze nonessential eval changes; run an extended 48‑hour soak on preprod
- Redwood: deliver quantized model build and a temporary rate‑limit profile to reduce tail conditions

I attached the MAP (Mutual_Action_Plan_v3.xlsx) with named owners and week‑by‑week checkpoints, plus a short risk appendix. Immediate asks: please confirm by EOD Monday whether you want us to pursue Option A or Option B and confirm a single procurement contact for the PO.
